findings.summary: The base URL is validated as loopback, but fetch follows redirects by default. A local endpoint can redirect any request, including synthetic trade-update fixture POST bodies and the marker query, to a non-loopback host, so the verifier does not guarantee loopback-only traffic.
findings.recommendation: Set redirect: error for every fetch (including rawRequest), or validate every redirect target as loopback before following it; add a regression check that a loopback redirect is rejected without contacting the destination.

checks.loopback_target_validation: PASS: accepts only http and exact loopback hostnames and rejects URL credentials/query/fragment in the base URL
checks.secret_hygiene: PASS: no real credentials; trace-query-secret-sentinel is an explicit benign sentinel and output checks ensure query redaction
checks.fixture_ids_values: PASS: local-* IDs and fixed AAPL values are synthetic fixtures
checks.reset_cleanup: PASS WITH LIMIT: successful path resets at end and catch path attempts reset while preserving original error
checks.account_assertions: PASS: compares positions and openOrders before and after trade-update observation
checks.live_broker_traffic: FAIL: implicit fetch redirect can send synthetic data to non-loopback destination
